title: Generic splitting extends to the finite étale section cover on the original open
statement: Let S be a normal integral scheme and c:C→S a morphism with section σ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let q:Cη→Spec k(S) and j:Cη→C be the generic-fibre pullback square [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let sη:Spec k(S)→Cη satisfy sηq=id and sηj=aησ. Let G be a finite group and Z→Cη a finite étale G-torsor with a k(S)-rational point over sη. Let U⊂S contain the generic point. Suppose jU:Cη→C_U factors j, PA→C_U is finite étale, and ψ:Z→PA forms a pullback square with jU. For any b:U→C_U with b followed by the open inclusion equal to U→S followed by σ, there is an isomorphism ∐_G U≅PA×_{C_U}U over U. No smoothness, Noetherian, local stalk, normalization or power-series hypotheses are needed.

source.place: Tag 0EYJ, splitting of the section fibre; Tag 0BQM, full faithfulness at the generic point.

proof.text: The open U is nonempty because it contains the generic point. Its generic point is the subtype point η of S. The map k:Spec k(U) → Spec k(S) induced by the stalk map of U → S satisfies k;aη=aU;ιU. Pick the rational point z in hZ and put r=k;z. Cancel the monomorphism C_U → C in the section compatibility equations to obtain (r;πZ);jU=aU;b. The torsor identity, composed with pullback symmetry, has components (id,smul g). Apply the proved FinitaryPreExtensive.isIso_sigmaDesc_lift_comp to base change it along r; this gives a splitting ∐_G Spec k(U) ≅ Z ×_{Cη} Spec k(U), over Spec k(U). Universality of finite coproducts similarly identifies the generic fibre of ∐_G U with ∐_G Spec k(U). Paste the pullback square for ψ with the rational section fibre, and paste the two canonical squares defining the generic fibre of PA ×_{C_U} U. The equation just proved gives a common cospan. Its canonical pullback isomorphism, composed with the two splittings, is an isomorphism between the generic fibres of the two covers over Spec k(U).

The local rings of U are integrally closed by transport through the stalk isomorphisms of its open immersion. Both covers are finite etale: the constant cover uses IsFinite.sigmaDesc and locality of etaleness; the section cover is a base change of PA. Apply finiteEtale_normalIntegral_generic_hom_full over U to the generic isomorphism and its inverse to obtain f and g over U. For f;g, apply uniqueness in that same theorem to the generic identity of the constant cover; its compatibility equation follows by composing the two extension equations and cancelling the generic inverse pair. The identity itself has the same compatibility, so f;g=id. Repeat over the section cover to get g;f=id. These maps form the claimed scheme isomorphism, and the over-U equation from the first extension is precisely the required projection equation.

lean.statement:
theorem GaloisCover.section_finiteEtale_generic_split {S C : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsIntegral S] (hS : ∀ x : S, IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x))
    (c : C ⟶ S)
    (σ : S ⟶ C) (hσ : σ ≫ c = 𝟙 S)
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G]
    {Cη : Scheme.{u}} (q : Cη ⟶ Spec S.functionField) (j : Cη ⟶ C)
    (hCη : IsPullback q j (S.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint S)) c)
    (sη : Spec S.functionField ⟶ Cη) (hsq : sη ≫ q = 𝟙 _)
    (hsj : sη ≫ j = S.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint S) ≫ σ)
    (Z : GaloisCover G Cη) (hZ : ∃ z : Spec S.functionField ⟶ Z.P, z ≫ Z.π = sη)
    (U : S.Opens) (hηU : genericPoint S ∈ U)
    (jU : Cη ⟶ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme) (PA : (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.FiniteEtale)
    (ψ : Z.P ⟶ PA.obj.left) (hjU : jU ≫ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι = j)
    (hψ : IsPullback ψ Z.π PA.obj.hom jU)
    (b : U.toScheme ⟶ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme)
    (hb : b ≫ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι = U.ι ≫ σ) :
    ∃ e : (∐ fun _ : G ↦ U.toScheme) ≅ pullback PA.obj.hom b,
      e.hom ≫ pullback.snd PA.obj.hom b = Sigma.desc (fun _ : G ↦ 𝟙 U.toScheme)
